tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.summary: Deploy of v2.3.1 to production caused checkout-api to fail health checks with an 18% error rate across all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Per runbook, service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. First rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error) leaving us-east on v2.3.0 and us-west/eu-west on v2.3.1; a retry completed the rollout. Verified post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.2%. Root cause of v2.3.1 failure pending investigation; v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging (seq 2), so it likely regressed before production.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

**Rollback:**
1. Checked deployment history: `v2.3.1` (latest deploy) was unhealthy in production; `v2.3.0` was the most recent healthy production release.
2. Current state confirmed `v2.3.1` deployed in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
3. First rollback attempt partially failed with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 but us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1.
4. Retried the rollback, which completed successfully — all three regions are now on `v2.3.0`.

**Verification:** checkout-api is now healthy in all regions with the error rate back down to 0.2%.

**Incident:** The `create_incident` call initially returned a timeout, but I verified via `list_incidents` that the SEV2 incident **INC-0001** ("checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0") was actually created and is open. It documents the full rollback process, the partial failure and retry, and the verified post-rollback state.

Note for follow-up: `v2.3.1-rc` was also unhealthy in staging (seq 2), suggesting the regression existed before production — worth investigating before any re-deploy of v2.3.1.
